MVC, MVP, MVVM, MVI, UDF and MV all query the same simulated weather. Open one, then read its module next to the others.

Responsibilities, data flow, state, testability and when to use each
Official pages define unidirectional data flow, UI state and state holders; MVC, MVP, MVVM, MVI and MV are community names.

The Activity is View and Controller at once
The Activity is both View and Controller: it reads input, calls the Model and updates the Views directly.
click -> Activity -> Model; Model -> Activity -> Views
In the Views
Robolectric (the logic is inside the Activity)
A tiny screen or a prototype
The Presenter holds the logic, the View is passive
The Activity (View) shows state and forwards clicks; the Presenter calls the Model and drives the View through an interface, with no Android dependency.
click -> Activity -> Presenter -> Model; Model -> Presenter -> View interface -> Activity
In the Presenter and the Views
Plain JVM: a fake View and a fake Model
Testable logic without Jetpack; existing MVP code
The ViewModel exposes a StateFlow of UiState
The Activity renders one UiState; the ViewModel calls the Model and exposes it as a StateFlow.
click -> Activity -> ViewModel -> Model; Model -> ViewModel -> StateFlow(UiState) -> Activity renders
StateFlow in the ViewModel
Plain JVM: the ViewModel with a fake Model
The default for View-based apps
One state, intents in, a pure reducer
One immutable State. Actions become Intents, a pure Reducer computes the next State, one-shot Effects go through a Channel (a community pattern, not an official term).
click -> Intent -> ViewModel -> Change -> Reducer -> new State -> Activity renders (+ Effect -> Toast)
One immutable State in the ViewModel\'s StateFlow
Plain JVM: the Reducer without coroutines; the ViewModel with a fake Model
Complex screens with many events and one state to audit
The official Compose shape: state down, events up
The shape the official guide describes: the ViewModel exposes StateFlow<UiState>, a stateless content composable sits below the screen, events are method calls.
click -> onQuery -> ViewModel.query() -> Model; Model -> StateFlow(UiState) -> collectAsStateWithLifecycle -> recompose
StateFlow<UiState> in the ViewModel
Plain JVM: the ViewModel with a fake Model
The default for new Compose code
State lives in a plain holder, no ViewModel
No ViewModel: a plain state holder class kept by rememberSaveable, read directly by the composables (a community name, not an official term; not the official choice for screen-level state).
click -> onQuery -> WeatherHolder.query() -> Model; Model -> mutableStateOf -> recompose
mutableStateOf in a plain class kept by rememberSaveable
Plain JVM: the holder with a test scope
Small, self-contained screens. A finished result survives rotation, a query in flight does not
